messages:
Rachel (ACME): Hey team — started seeing big latency + occasional 500s on our prod inference calls since ~10:05 PST yesterday. p50 looks fine but p95 jumped. Sample request ids: r-abc123, r-abc124, r-abc125. Tokens ~1100-1300. Can you help collect a repro pack? :sad:

Alice (Support): Sorry about that, Rachel. We'll start collecting repro info. First ask: can you run a quick curl reproducer with the exact headers you send and paste the curl output + the x-request-id header? Also, please run the debug bundle command below and upload the tarball (details after).

Alice (Support): Example curl we usually ask customers to run (replace API_KEY and PAYLOAD):

```bash
curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "x-request-id: r-abc123" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood/gpt-medium-v1","input":"<short prompt>","max_tokens":1200}'
```

Ben (Oncall): @devon_engineer heads-up: looks like multi-tenant queueing could be a factor. Ask Rachel to include these in the debug bundle: list of request ids (she already started), the client-side concurrency & RPS, and a timeline (UTC). From infra side we need serving logs spanning the incident window and runtime traces for the matching request ids.

Devon (Engineer): For reproducibility I recommend a small repro pack we generate here:
- prompt_set: 20 prompts (mix short/long), token targets: 200, 600, 1200.
- concurrency profile: spike test -> steady at 40 concurrency for 6 minutes, ramp to 80 for 30s, back down.
- clients: 8 parallel clients, each issuing requests with an inter-arrival Poisson process (mean 50ms).

Devon (Engineer): Script we use internally to record client-side repros (example, replace KEY):

```bash
# run 8 clients in parallel, each does 200 requests per minute
for i in {1..8}; do 
  (seq 1 200 | xargs -I{} -P0 curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer KEY" \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -H "x-request-id: repro-${i}-$(date +%s%3N)" \
    -d '{"model":"redwood/gpt-medium-v1","input":"prompt_${i}","max_tokens":600}' >/tmp/repro-${i}.log 2>&1)&
done
wait
```

Cathy (SRE): On our side, please ask Rachel to run this debug collector (no root needed, runs in userland):

```bash
# collect request-specific logs and env info
sudo /opt/redwood/bin/collect_debug --request-ids r-abc123,r-abc124,r-abc125 --window "2024-11-12T17:50:00Z/2024-11-12T18:10:00Z" --out /tmp/debug-176999.tar.gz
```

Cathy (SRE): If sudo isn't allowed, at minimum gather:
- client curl output including response headers (x-request-id, x-trace-id)
- /var/log/redwood/runtime.log lines for those request ids (tail -n 500)
- /etc/redwood/serving.conf

Alice (Support): We'll provide a secure upload link once you have the tarball. Also include a small sample of your prompt set (20 prompts) and specify which prompts produced the 500s. For prompt sets, please annotate token counts (tokenizers vary); we only need rough counts: e.g., prompt_7 -> 1,230 tokens.

Rachel (ACME): OK I'm running the curl examples now and collecting logs. FYI our client sends a small batcher in front of the API that opens 60 concurrent sockets during traffic peaks — maybe relevant. Uploading debug tar to the secure link in a minute.

Repro-bot: New debug bundle created: debug-176999.tar.gz (size 18MB) — ID: dbg-9f7c. Uploaded to s3://redwood-support-uploads/dbg-9f7c (private).

Ben (Oncall): Great, thanks. Devon/Cathy — once we have the bundle can you run the internal repro harness against the same model + quantization profile? Key things to test:
- same model: redwood/gpt-medium-v1 (quantized-int8)
- KV cache warm vs cold behavior for long sequences
- concurrency = 40 steady and a short 80-concurrency spike
- token window: 600-1300

Devon (Engineer): Will do. I'll generate a small latency repro pack (tar.gz) with: promptset.json, concurrency_profile.json, client_run.sh, expected_response_ids.txt. I'll also add a step to include `--x-request-id` mapping so we can correlate.

Alice (Support): Rachel — once we confirm a repro internally we'll either provide a curl-based minimal repro you can run, or ask for a short change on your side to reproduce at will. Thanks for the quick upload, we'll follow up with a timeline and next steps within 2 business hours. :thumbsup:

Rachel (ACME): Thank you all — appreciate the quick turnaround. I'll stand by to run more repros if you need them.

Cathy (SRE): Quick note for the internal run: watch for `shard=shard-7` backpressure and any `batcher queue full` warnings in runtime.log — those were correlated with past p95 spikes.

Ben (Oncall): Marking this as escalated -> SRE priority P1 (latency/500s affecting customer).

Alice (Support): Closing loop for now, will update thread once we have a deterministic repro or find root cause.
